patients.label: 83-year-old man with choroidal melanoma of the left eye complicated by macular hole and vitreous hemorrhage after radiotherapy

identity_evidence.quote: An 83-year-old man was referred to our hospital with suspected serous retinal detachment in his left eye.

attribution_limitations: The authors presume the posterior vitreous detachment may have been caused by chronic tumor-related vitreous inflammation or floating blood cells, or may be age-related; these are hedged mechanisms, not asserted causes.
The authors considered the vitreous hemorrhage a consequence of acute ischemic shrinkage of the tumor after radiotherapy; this is a hedged interpretation and is not recorded as an asserted cause.
The Discussion says the timing of vitrectomy was 6 months after tumor radiotherapy without saying whether this is the first or second vitrectomy; it is not attached to either procedure.
The authors state the melanoma site was distant from the macula, ruling out radiation-induced macular hole. This author reasoning is not recorded as a fact or as a refuted diagnosis.

Table 1 current-case cells (initial visual acuity, tumor location, base, thickness, color) restate the initial findings and are cited with the text as the same measurements; the table names no method or date.
The Discussion cites "the surgical finding of bleeding from the tumor surface" without saying which of the two vitrectomies; it is not attached to either procedure event.

evidence.quote: Clinical course of the patient with choroidal melanoma.

(A) Ultra-wide-field fundus photography revealed a white, elevated choroidal tumor with a central dark brown speckle (arrow) in the nasal quadrant and posterior vitreous detachment (arrowhead) inferior to the optic nerve.
(B) Fluorescein angiography showed early hyperfluorescence corresponding to the mass.
(C) Indocyanine green angiography showed blocked fluorescence and a small hyperfluorescent area at the edge.
(D) Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a hyperintense tumor (arrow) with a smooth border on axial T1 imaging-fast spin-echo.
(E) Iodine-123 isopropyl iodoamphetamine brain single-photon emission computed tomography showed high uptake in his left eye (arrow).
(A) Five months after radiotherapy, a full-thickness macular hole with cystic cavities was shown on optical coherence tomography.
(B) A further 2 weeks later, a massive vitreous hemorrhage appeared on ultra-wide-field fundus photography.
(C) The macular hole was successfully closed after pars plana vitrectomy with internal limiting membrane peeling.
